subtopics.title: P4M Summit at the 81st UNGA
subtopics.summary: India's External Affairs Minister co-chaired the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa, on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA in New York. The P4M framework is built upon the Carney Doctrine on middle-power solidarity. It is designed as an open and flexible framework rather than an exclusive bloc, and it seeks to strengthen international law, peace, multilateral cooperation and inclusive prosperity.

UNGA theme: Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All
P4M co-chaired by India's External Affairs Minister and European Council President Antonio Costa

subtopics.title: India's Position on Reformed Multilateralism
subtopics.summary: India argued that disruptions in fuel, food, fertiliser and finance hit developing countries and the Global South disproportionately. It linked supply-chain risks to a call for de-risking and diversification. India also called for greater representation of developing countries, more inclusive decision-making, transparency and comprehensive reform of the UN Security Council, and for guardrails on emerging technologies.
facts: 4F crisis: disruptions involving Fuel, Food, Fertiliser and Finance
4F disruptions have a disproportionate impact on developing countries and the Global South
Supply-chain risks: disruptions, strategic chokepoints and excessive economic dependencies
Called for de-risking and diversification to build more resilient global supply chains
Geopolitical fragmentation and strategic competition put existing multilateral institutions under pressure
Called for greater representation of developing countries and greater transparency in global institutions
Pursues UNSC reform through the G4 and L.69 groupings
Called for international frameworks and guardrails for AI, space security and digital technologies

subtopics.title: Visegrad Group (V4)
subtopics.summary: The Visegrad Group is a regional cooperation grouping of four Central European countries, established in 1991 after the end of the Cold War and the collapse of the Soviet bloc. All four members belong to both the European Union and NATO. At the V4 plus India meeting, the V4 unanimously supported India's candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council.
facts: Named after Visegrad, a town in Hungary
Established in 1991 after the end of the Cold War and the collapse of the Soviet bloc
Members: Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia
All four members are members of both the EU and NATO
Cooperation covers political and diplomatic coordination, defence and security
Cooperation also covers economic cooperation, energy and culture
Unanimously supported India's candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council

subtopics.title: US-Denmark-Greenland Agreement and Greenland's Strategic Role
subtopics.summary: A trilateral security agreement among the United States, Denmark and Greenland was signed on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA. It builds on the 1951 US-Denmark Defence Agreement, expands US activities in Greenland and restricts military presence by non-NATO states through joint approval. It does not transfer sovereignty over Greenland and recognises Greenland's right to self-determination.
facts: Signed by the United States, Denmark and Greenland on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA
Builds on the 1951 US-Denmark Defence Agreement while reaffirming Greenland's right to self-determination
Expands activities at Pituffik Space Base, formerly Thule Air Base
US military access to Narsarsuaq (southern Greenland) and Mestersvig (eastern Greenland)
Restricts military presence by non-NATO states through joint approval
Does not transfer sovereignty over Greenland to the United States
Greenland lies within the GIUK gap, a key chokepoint for monitoring North Atlantic naval movements
Large untapped rare earth reserves; Transpolar Sea Route opening as Arctic ice melts

subtopics.title: Arctic Council
subtopics.summary: The Arctic Council is an inter-governmental platform established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration. It provides a forum for discussion and cooperation on the Arctic environment and sustainable development, with its main focus on climate change and its impact on the Arctic region. Eight Arctic nations are members, and India has been an observer since 2013.
facts: Type: inter-governmental platform
Established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration
Purpose: forum for cooperation on the Arctic environment and sustainable development
Main focus: climate change and its impact on the Arctic region
Members: Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden and the United States
Chairmanship alternates every 2 years; current chair is Denmark (2025-2027)
India has been an observer since 2013
India's first Arctic research station, Himadri (2008), is at Ny-Alesund, Svalbard, Norway

quizzes.passage: The 81st United Nations General Assembly opened on 8 September 2026 in New York, under the theme "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All." On its sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister co-chaired the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa. The P4M framework is built on the middle-power solidarity idea that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney set out at Davos. It was conceived in response to the erosion of global consensus, trade weaponisation and escalating conflicts across Europe and West Asia. Leaders of the European Union, Brazil, Kenya and Canada conceptualised the initiative, and India, Australia and Barbados co-sponsored it. It is designed as an open and flexible framework rather than another exclusive bloc or permanent bureaucracy. Its aims include strengthening international law, peace, multilateral cooperation and prosperity. It also seeks to enable countries from different political traditions to cooperate on reforming multilateral institutions and on common global challenges. At the same sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister took part in the 1st V4 plus India Foreign Ministers' Meeting, held during the Assembly week. India's position on reformed multilateralism was presented within this wider setting. The booklet presents the summit as one of the main events of the Assembly week.

quizzes.passage: The Arctic has moved up the international agenda as melting ice opens new maritime corridors, including the Transpolar Sea Route. Control and influence over Arctic sea lanes are expected to shape future global trade and naval power projection. China describes itself as a near-Arctic state and is investing in Arctic research and infrastructure, while Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline. The United States views Greenland as central to countering both. Greenland, the world's largest island, lies between North America and Europe, which gives it a strategic position for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic. Pituffik Space Base, formerly known as Thule Air Base, is a US facility for monitoring potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea. Denmark's firm stance highlights the tension between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers. Within this wider competition, the Arctic Council is a platform through which countries discuss the region. Its members are the countries whose territory lies inside the Arctic area, and countries from outside the region also take part in its work. The Council gives these countries a place to talk through issues affecting the Arctic. Its discussions are reported in the booklet's coverage of Arctic affairs. Its members are not the only states with an interest in the region.

quizzes.passage: The Arctic has moved up the international agenda as melting ice opens new maritime corridors, including the Transpolar Sea Route. These routes could reduce travel time between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, lower fuel and shipping costs, and bypass the Panama and Suez canals. Great powers are competing for influence in the region, and China describes itself as a near-Arctic state. Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline, while the United States regards Greenland as central to countering both. Greenland lies between North America and Europe, a position that makes it significant for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic. Pituffik Space Base, formerly known as Thule Air Base, is a US facility for monitoring potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea. Denmark's firm stance highlights the tension between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers. The Arctic Council is a forum through which countries discuss the region's environment and development. Its members are the countries whose territory lies inside the Arctic area, and countries from outside the region also take part in its work. Denmark has indicated that the arrangement could support a sustained NATO role in Greenland and the wider Arctic. The Council also has a secretariat, which the booklet mentions in its coverage of the body.
